title: Interchange
text:
Conversion to and from the Hypergraph Interchange Format (HIF)
HIF is a JSON standard for exchanging higher-order networks between libraries e.g. XGI and HyperNetX (Coll et al., 2025, Network Science 13; arXiv:2507.11520). The JSON schema in parag/data/hif_schema.json is from the HIF-standard repository (MIT License).
from parag.io import to_hif, from_hif, validate_hif, write_hif, read_hif

title: Interchange
text:
Examples
Round trip of the network communities (undirected), in both modes, and reading by XGI.

G = nx.karate_club_graph()
nodes = (
    pd.Series({i: list(t) for i, t in enumerate(list(nx.community.girvan_newman(G))[3])})
    .explode()
    .to_frame("node id")
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={"index": "community id"})
    .astype({"node id": int})
    .loc[:, ["node id", "community id"]]
)
edges = pd.DataFrame(G.edges, columns=["source", "target"])
for mode in ["subsets", "pairwise"]:
    hif = to_hif(nodes, edges, "node id", "source", "target", "community id", mode=mode)
    assert validate_hif(hif)
    d = from_hif(json.loads(json.dumps(hif)))
    pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(d["nodes"], nodes, check_dtype=False)
    pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(d["edges"], edges, check_dtype=False)
    H = xgi.convert.from_hif_dict(hif)
    assert H.num_nodes == len(nodes)
    assert H.num_edges == (nodes["community id"].nunique() if mode == "subsets" else len(edges))

Directed pairwise edges (drug → side effect), and writing/reading a HIF file.

edges = pd.read_csv("inputs/ChSe-Decagon_monopharmacy.csv")
nodes = pd.concat(
    [
        edges.loc[:, ["# STITCH"]].drop_duplicates().rename(columns={"# STITCH": "node id"}).assign(subset="drug"),
        edges.loc[:, ["Individual Side Effect", "Side Effect Name"]]
        .drop_duplicates(subset=["Individual Side Effect"])
        .rename(columns={"Individual Side Effect": "node id"})
        .assign(subset="side effect"),
    ],
    axis=0,
    ignore_index=True,
)
hif = to_hif(nodes, edges, "node id", "# STITCH", "Individual Side Effect", "subset", mode="pairwise", directed=True)
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as dir_path:
    d = from_hif(read_hif(write_hif(hif, f"{dir_path}/drugs.json")))
pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(d["nodes"], nodes, check_dtype=False)
pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(d["edges"], edges, check_dtype=False)
assert type(xgi.convert.from_hif_dict(hif)).__name__ == "DiHypergraph"

A HIF written by another library (XGI), with nodes in multiple hyperedges.

hif = dict(xgi.convert.to_hif_dict(xgi.Hypergraph([[1, 2, 3], [3, 4], [4, 5, 6, 7]])))
try:
    from_hif(hif)
    raise AssertionError("expected a ValueError")
except ValueError:
    pass
d = from_hif(hif, subset_rule="largest")
assert d["nodes"]["subset"].tolist() == [0, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 2]
assert len(d["edges"]) == 3 + 1 + 6  # g: clique expansion
assert from_hif(hif, subset_rule="first")["nodes"]["subset"].tolist() == [0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 2]

Invalid HIF.

assert not validate_hif({"nodes": []}, errors="warn")

title: parag
section: Interpretation as a hypergraph, using proportion of degrees by communities
text:
Interpretation as a hypergraph, using proportion of degrees by communities
Proportion of degrees by communities in a pairwise graph helps reveal how nodes are grouped together and connected within different communities. This analysis highlights clusters of nodes with strong internal connections, potentially representing higher-order relationships. By comparing the degree proportions within and between communities, we can distinguish internal cohesion from inter-community interactions. These insights aid in interpreting the graph as a hypergraph, where communities with high intra-community connections may signify higher-order relationships, offering a richer understanding of complex interactions beyond simple pairwise connections.
Inspired by

Vehlow, Corinna, Thomas Reinhardt, and Daniel Weiskopf. “Visualizing fuzzy overlapping communities in networks.” IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics 19.12 (2013): 2486-2495.
Figure 9B

Interoperability with other hypergraph libraries
Nodes and edges can be converted to and from the Hypergraph Interchange Format (HIF), e.g. to exchange data with XGI or HyperNetX. With mode='subsets' (default), the subsets (e.g. communities) are the hyperedges; with mode='pairwise', each edge is a hyperedge of 2 nodes.

from parag.io import to_hif, from_hif
hif = to_hif(
    nodes,
    edges,
    col_node_id='node id',
    col_source='source',
    col_target='target',
    col_subset_id='community id',
)
## e.g. write_hif(hif, 'communities.json'), xgi.read_hif('communities.json')
## from HIF, e.g. from_hif(read_hif('communities.json')), input for to_net
d = from_hif(hif)
d['nodes'].head(2)

Data sources and acknowledgements
The gene-interaction and drug side-effect examples use datasets from the BioSNAP collection. To keep the examples (and CI) fast and independent of network access, only the first 1000 lines of each file are stored in examples/inputs; see the README there for details.
